entry.name: jit.playlist
entry.description: Use jit.playlist to organize sets of video files and play them back. Each video is given a visual representation in a clip where a selection from the entire video file may be choosen. Clips may be dragged within a jit.playlist to re-order them, or they maybe dragged to other jit.playlist objects by using the handle (dot) on the left side of the clip.

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Drag and drop compatible media files
messages.description: Create a newobject by dragging and dropping a compatible media file into an unlocked patch. To load additional media files into aobject, drag the new file onto theUI until a line appears above or below the currently loaded file. To rearrange tracks within, click and drag the handle (dot on the left side) up or down in a locked patch. To replace a currently loaded file, drag the new file over the old one until the entire track is highlighted.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Press play, loop, and make selections
messages.description: Use your mouse to play and stop a clip in. Also use it to select small parts of the sample for playback.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Add a new video file to the list
messages.description: Add a new video file to the list. First argument specifies the video file. Second (optional) argument specifies the slot number for the clip (starting at 1). If no arguments are listed, clicking the append message in a locked patcher will open a dialog box where you can choose a file to append.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Remove all clips from the playlist. To remove just one clip, right-click on the file you wish to remove in a locked patcher and choose "Remove" from the contextual menu.

messages.name: getclipattr
messages.digest: Retrieve attribute state for a specific clip
messages.description: The word, followed by a clip number and attribute name, will send that attribute's value out the notification (middle) outlet of. This allows you to retrieve an attribute state for a specific clip. You can retrieve read-only attributes (e.g. duration, moviedim, etc.), along with most attributes supported by.

messages.name: getcontent
messages.digest: Get the contents and behavior of all clips
messages.description: The wordsends the contents and behavior of all clips out the last outlet ofin dictionary format. Connect the last outlet to aobject to see the contents. Please note that most content states will not print their default values. These will only be printed if you explicitly set a value. For the "absolutepath" entry, the full file path for each clip will only be displayed if the file is not in Max's search path. If the file is in Max's search path, only the file name will be displayed.

messages.name: int
messages.description: 0 stops video playback. A number greater than zero begins playback of the clip with that index. Indices begin counting at 1.

messages.name: next
messages.description: Plays the next clip loaded in.

messages.name: pause
messages.description: Pause playback of the current clip at the current position.

messages.name: remove
messages.description: The word, followed by a clip number starting at 1, removes that clip from the list.

messages.name: resume
messages.description: Resume playback from the current position if playback has been paused.

messages.name: selection
messages.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip
messages.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip using a normalized range (0.0 is the beginning, 1.0 is the end). The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in jit.playlist. If only one argument is given, it serves as the clip number and clears any selection from that clip.

messages.name: selectionms
messages.digest: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds
messages.description: Select playback endpoints for a clip in milliseconds. The first argument specifies which clip (starting at 1). The second argument is the start point for the clip, and the third argument is the end point. If only two arguments are given, they serve as the start and end points for all clips in jit.playlist. If only one argument is given, it serves as the end point for all clips in jit.playlist.

messages.name: setclip
messages.digest: Set an attribute state for a specific clip
messages.description: attributes are available in jit.playlist. To control a specific clip, use the "setclip" message followed by the clip number, attribute name, and value. The message "setclip 2 loop 1" will turn looping on for clip 2.
